channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Six Projects with Japanese Investment Valued at 14 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to implement six projects involving Japanese companies, with a total investment of 14 billion tenge. These projects span mechanical engineering, chemical, and mining industries. The Ministry of Industry confirmed the plans, which include the opening of a vehicle repair complex and the development of various specialized equipment.

item.title: Fifteen Dead Caspian Seals Found on Mangystau Coast; Experts Investigating Water Quality
item.description: Fifteen dead Caspian seals have been discovered along the coast of the Mangystau region. Specialists are currently collecting biological samples and water from the Caspian Sea to determine the cause of death. This follows a previous incident in April where 97 seals were found dead.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Digital Infrastructure with New Data Center in Ekibastuz
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing its artificial intelligence sector by constructing a data processing center in Ekibastuz, Pavlodar region. The country has already launched the Alem.Cloud supercomputer and AI-Farabium cluster. Venture investments in AI projects grew significantly between 2023 and 2025, supporting over 100 AI startups and indicating a maturing tech market.

item.title: Tajikistan's Withdrawal from ICC: Gains and Losses Explored
item.description: Tajikistan's decision to withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC) is examined for its potential gains and losses. Dilrabo Samadova suggests the move does not absolve Tajikistan of past obligations. The article delves into the implications of this withdrawal.

item.title: Afghanistan Seeks International Aid for Climate Change and Disaster Mitigation
item.description: Afghanistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, called for fair international financial and technical assistance to combat climate change. He highlighted that Afghanistan suffers severe consequences from climate change despite minimal contribution to greenhouse gas emissions. Baradar urged against political interference in climate action and stressed shared responsibility for global climate protection.

item.title: Kazakhstan's VAT Revenue Falls Short of Expectations by Hundreds of Billions of Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's budget deficit reached approximately 2.9 trillion tenge in the first nine months of 2026. Value Added Tax (VAT) revenues were nearly 686 billion tenge below the planned amount. Total revenues were 16.53 trillion tenge against expenditures of 18.74 trillion tenge. Non-oil deficit also exceeded projections.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tenge Projected to Devalue to 523 per Dollar by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's tenge is forecast to weaken against the US dollar, reaching 523-587 tenge per dollar between 2027 and 2029, according to the Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development (EFSD). The national currency's strengthening is attributed to rising commodity prices and foreign investor demand for Kazakh government bonds. Economic growth is projected at 5% for 2026-2027.

item.title: Almaty Needs New Mountain Resorts: Existing Infrastructure Insufficient, Experts Say
item.description: Almaty requires new mountain resorts beyond upgrading existing ones, with the proposed Almaty SuperSki project in Kokzhailau and Kumbel peaks highlighted. The project aims for over 60 km of ski slopes and year-round tourist infrastructure. Economist Almas Chukin notes current accessibility issues, especially in spring and autumn, making new developments necessary.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints 'Kazakhtelecom' Operator for National Video Monitoring System
item.description: Kazakhstan has designated JSC 'Kazakhtelecom' as the operator for its national video monitoring system, according to a government decree. This decision, effective October 19, aligns with the cybersecurity law. The system aims to enhance public order, combat crime, and ensure citizen safety through widespread video surveillance.

item.title: Belgian King and Queen Visit Kazakhstan to Discuss Scientific Developments and Mineral Cooperation
item.description: Belgium's King Philippe and Queen Mathilde visited Kazakhstan, engaging in discussions with the Kazakh government on cooperation in the field of critical minerals. A roundtable meeting focused on these minerals, fostering collaboration between Kazakh and Belgian scientific and business communities. The visit aims to implement agreements reached between the leaders of both nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Lowering Retirement Age for Women Following Citizen Appeals
item.description: A movement advocating for women's retirement age reduction in Kazakhstan has appealed to a Member of Parliament. Discussions were held with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection regarding current pension norms and the arguments for lowering the age. The ministry noted that pension benefits are linked to contribution periods and duration in the system.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Diversify Arms Procurement Away from Russia
item.description: Central Asian countries are increasingly seeking arms from India, China, Turkey, and European states to reduce dependence on Russia. Experts suggest this diversification offers political freedom but presents challenges in managing varied weapon systems. India has reportedly supplied Akash air defense systems to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.

item.title: King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium Visit National Museum of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev accompanied King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium, on a state visit, to the National Museum. The royal couple admired the museum's architecture and exhibits showcasing the cultural and historical heritage of the Great Steppe, with particular interest in the Golden Hall.

item.title: Tokayev Visits National Museum with Belgian King and Queen
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev visited the National Museum accompanied by the King and Queen of Belgium. The visit occurred during the Belgian royals' state visit to Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Loses Up to 40 Billion Tenge Due to Illegal Tobacco
item.description: Kazakhstan is experiencing financial losses of up to 40 billion tenge annually as a result of the illegal tobacco market. This figure was stated by Denis Efimov.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explores Green Hydrogen and Ammonia Production Projects with International Partners
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing several green hydrogen and ammonia production projects with foreign companies. The HYRASIA ONE project in the Mangystau region, in partnership with a German firm, aims for an initial output of 130,000 tons of hydrogen and 725,000 tons of ammonia annually, with potential for significant scaling.

item.title: Tajikistan Ratifies UN Convention Against Cybercrime to Enhance International Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's parliament has ratified the UN Convention against Cybercrime, enabling law enforcement agencies to cooperate with other countries in combating cybercrimes and exchanging electronic evidence. This ratification aims to strengthen efforts against transnational cyber threats, which have been increasing in the country.

item.title: King of Belgium Impressed by Kazakhstan's Vision for Transforming Mineral Resources into New Industry
item.description: King Philippe of Belgium expressed deep admiration for Kazakhstan's vision to transform its mineral resources into a future industry during a Kazakh-Belgian roundtable. He highlighted the importance of critical minerals and offered Belgium's expertise in science-industry cooperation to develop this potential.

item.title: 1C Assures Kazakhstan Users of Data Security Amidst Russian Datacenter Concerns
item.description: Software company 1C has reassured its Kazakhstan-based clients that their data infrastructure is entirely located within the republic. This clarification comes in response to user concerns about potential disruptions to businesses if Russian data centers face attacks. 1C stated that both cloud and local infrastructure, as well as product development, are handled by Kazakh specialists.

item.title: Five Members of Drug Group Sentenced to Up to 17 Years in Prison in Astana
item.description: Five members of an organized criminal group involved in systematic drug trafficking through a Telegram channel have been sentenced to up to 17 years in prison in Astana. The group operated approximately two thousand drug caches and had a turnover exceeding 90 million tenge. Police seized over 165 grams of marijuana and cannabis resin during their arrest.

item.title: IAEA Mission in Astana to Prepare for Nuclear Power Plant Infrastructure Assessment
item.description: An IAEA mission is in Astana from October 12-15 to assist Kazakhstan in preparing for a comprehensive assessment of its nuclear power plant construction infrastructure. Experts are discussing a national self-assessment report and defining next steps before the main Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review (INIR) mission. Kazakhstan plans to build several nuclear power plants, with the first, "Balkhash," to be located near Ulken village in Almaty region.

item.title: Saneg Company's Oil Field Licenses in Uzbekistan Canceled Due to Non-Compliance
item.description: Licenses previously granted to Saneg company for oil field operations in Uzbekistan have been revoked due to failure to meet contractual obligations. The Director of the State Assets Management Agency (DABA) stated that the fields themselves were not privatized, but the right to use the subsoil was licensed. The licensing procedure for hydrocarbon exploration has since shifted to an auction-based system.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank Raises 630 Million Yuan for Projects in Kazakhstan
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) has completed its debut Dim Sum bond issuance in Hong Kong, raising 630 million Chinese yuan. The three-year senior unsecured bonds, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, attracted demand exceeding supply by 2.5 times, with a final coupon rate of 3.9%. This issuance strengthens the EDB's position in Asian capital markets and provides a new source of yuan financing for projects.

item.title: Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region's GDP Reaches 1.5 Billion Somoni in Nine Months
item.description: The Gross Regional Product (GRP) of the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) reached 1 billion 509 million somoni in the first nine months of 2026, with an actual growth rate of 8%. Exports increased by 11.6% and paid services rose by 21.3% compared to the same period in 2025. Industrial production saw a 21.3% growth, and 40 new production facilities were launched, creating 153 jobs.

item.title: UNHCR Chief Urges Increased Support for Afghan Returnees and Protection of Girls' Rights
item.description: The UN High Commissioner for Refugees called for greater international investment to aid Afghan returnees, highlighting that millions are returning under difficult conditions, facing poverty, limited services, and restrictions on women and girls. The appeal was made during the 77th session of UNHCR’s Executive Committee.

item.title: Four Tax Officials Punished in Shymkent for Investor Interference
item.description: Four tax officials in Shymkent have been punished for illegally interfering with investors' activities. The prosecutor's office found that the state revenue department wrongly suspended a company's bank account operations. The responsible official was fined, and three other employees were also held administratively liable.

item.title: Legal Violations Found in State Procurements Worth Nearly 10 Billion Som in Six Regions
item.description: Legal violations have been identified in state procurements totaling nearly 10 billion som across six regions. In some cases, financial penalties were imposed, and mandatory instructions were issued to rectify the breaches. Further details are available through the provided link.

item.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Accuses Pakistani Party of Taking Instructions from Kabul
item.description: Faisal Karim Kundi, governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, accused Pakistan's PTI party of receiving political instructions from Kabul. He stated that the province's policies would now align with the federal government in Islamabad, not external sources. This follows repeated accusations by Pakistani officials against the Taliban.

item.title: Airlines Cancel Flights to Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns Following Houthi Attacks
item.description: Several regional and international airlines have canceled or suspended flights to Saudi Arabia due to increased security concerns following recent Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The airport was temporarily closed, causing significant disruptions to domestic and international flight schedules.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Strengthen Fight Against Shadow Lending Market
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to enhance mechanisms for combating illegal lending. The Agency for Financial Monitoring has proposed improvements to interest rate regulation, usury control, and identification of unlicensed lending activities to the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market.

item.title: Fifteen Seal Carcasses Found on Caspian Coast in Kazakhstan's Mangystau Region
item.description: Fifteen dead seals were discovered on the Caspian Sea coast in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region. The cause of death for the animals remains undetermined, though the Ministry of Agriculture stated that specialists are collecting water and soil samples. This follows a previous discovery of seals in the same area.

item.title: Afghanistan Disasters Claimed 679 Lives and Affected Over 44,000 Families in Past Year
item.description: Natural disasters killed 679 people and injured 1,634 across Afghanistan in the past year, according to the Taliban-run Afghanistan National Disaster Management Authority (ANDMA). The disasters affected 44,918 families, destroying thousands of homes, agricultural land, and infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and power networks.

item.title: Lithuanian PM Urges Zelensky to Strike Russian Data Centers for European Election Security
item.description: Lithuania's Prime Minister stated that striking Russian data centers could help protect European elections. The PM suggested that Ukraine's President Zelensky should be asked to increase attacks on these facilities. This statement highlights concerns about foreign interference in democratic processes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Claims Jailed Developer Planned Revolution with Criminal Groups
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated that jailed construction company founder Imamidin Tashov allegedly planned a revolution, seeking support from criminal elements, including crime boss Kamchy Kolbaev. Japarov made these remarks in response to Tashov's mother's appeal, asserting that his son was convicted on false charges. The president affirmed he cannot interfere with judicial processes but will consider a pardon request.

item.title: Newborn Missing from Dushanbe Maternity Hospital No. 1, Authorities Investigating
item.description: A newborn has gone missing from Dushanbe's first maternity hospital. The infant disappeared on the night of October 11-12. Authorities are currently conducting a search for the child. Further details are expected as the investigation progresses.

item.title: Scholarly Heritage of Transoxiana Presented at UNESCO Headquarters
item.description: An international conference on the scholarly heritage of Transoxiana was held at UNESCO headquarters in Paris, attended by over 300 scholars and diplomats. Participants discussed the contributions of Central Asian scholars to global civilization and the preservation of cultural heritage. The event was organized by the Center of Islamic Civilization in Uzbekistan and other partners.

item.title: Turkmenistan and EU Define Education Partnership Priorities Until 2034
item.description: Turkmenistan and the European Training Foundation (ETF) held a roundtable to define priorities for their education partnership until 2034. Discussions focused on modernizing vocational and higher education, digitalization, and developing skills in transport, logistics, energy, and digital communications. Joint action plans for 2028-2034 were outlined.

item.title: Individuals Arrested in Tashkent Region for Involving Minors in Drug Trafficking
item.description: Authorities in the Tashkent region have arrested individuals for recruiting underage girls into drug trafficking operations. During special operations in Chirchiq city and Qibray district, a total of 4.7 kg of narcotics were seized. Among those apprehended were university students. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Taliban Authority Reports 679 Fatalities from Natural Disasters in Afghanistan Over Past Year
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority reports 679 deaths and 1,634 injuries from natural disasters in the past year. The authority also stated that 4,470 homes were destroyed and 17,664 were partially damaged. The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed annually on October 13.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Minister Tells EU Envoy Global Community Failed to Support Farmers' Alternative Livelihoods
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, Afghanistan's acting foreign minister, told the EU special envoy that the international community has not sufficiently supported Afghan farmers with alternative livelihoods to combat narcotics. The EU envoy acknowledged Afghanistan's security and counter-narcotics achievements and pledged increased cooperation.
